title: Multiple linear regression
biology: Evolutionary biologists relate beetle horn length to body size and larval nutrition.
design: Sixty independent beetles are raised across a nutrient gradient and measured as adults.
data_characteristics: A conditional slope holding other predictors fixed
other_examples: Growth predicted by temperature and resources
Physiology predicted by size and treatment
Expression predicted by genotype and age
question: Does body size predict mean horn length after accounting for larval nutrition?
null: The body-size coefficient is zero conditional on nutrition in the specified model.
options: x1 * x2 also includes an interaction
anova(reduced, full) compares nested models fit to the same rows
assumptions: Correct mean pattern and residual spread
Strong predictor collinearity limits separate interpretation
parametric: Include a justified interaction or curved term
Use robust SEs/variance models for unequal error variance
nonparametric: A design-respecting permutation can test a specified effect
Separate rank correlations do not replace an adjusted regression

plot_args.note: Map nutrition to a continuous color scale
State response, predictor and color units

practice: What does holding nutrition fixed mean when interpreting the body-size coefficient?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1115)
body <- runif(60, 7, 12)
nutrition <- runif(60, 2, 10)
horn <- .4 + .35 * body + .16 * nutrition + rnorm(60, 0, .65)
d <- data.frame(beetle = 1:60, body_mm = body, nutrition_mg = nutrition, horn_mm = horn)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
p <- ggplot(d, aes(body_mm, horn_mm, color = nutrition_mg)) +
  geom_point(size = 3.8, alpha = .9) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#C8DCE0", high = "#174D58") +
  labs(x = "Adult body length (mm)", y = "Horn length (mm)", color = "Larval nutrition
(mg)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 18)
print(p)
code_analysis:
fit <- lm(horn_mm ~ body_mm + nutrition_mg, data = d)
reduced <- lm(horn_mm ~ nutrition_mg, data = d)
comparison <- anova(reduced, fit)
coefficients <- summary(fit)$coefficients
ci <- confint(fit)
generating_model: 60 independent body lengths are Uniform(7, 12) mm and nutrition values independently Uniform(2, 10) mg. Horn length = 0.4 + 0.35*body + 0.16*nutrition + Normal(0, 0.65 SD).
generating_truth: The true conditional body slope is 0.35 mm/mm and nutrition slope 0.16 mm/mg, with no interaction. Both zero-coefficient nulls are false.
teaching_point: Read each coefficient conditionally on the other variables in the stated model.
